Both these appeals are preferred by the claimants against the common judgment and award passed by the learned Land Reference Court, Jalna in Land Acquisition Reference Nos.126 of 2003 and 195 of 2000, dated 29.11.2008.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
The claimants' lands situated in Satona (Khurd), Tahsil Partur, Dist. Jalna, bearing block no.40,
admeasuring 3 H 30 R (3 24 R irrigated and 3 R barren); block no.39, admeasuring 3 H 58 R (3 H 56 R irrigated and 2 R barren); and block no.41, admeasuring 6 29 R, all irrigated, were acquired for "Lower Nimna Dudhana Project"
under one and the same acquisition proceedings pursuant to the notification dated 27.09.1994, issued and published under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Land Acquisition Officer 27-fa-759-2013+ awarded Rs.345/- for dry land.
The claimants received the inadequate compensation.
They preferred reference.

However,
Reference Court enhanced the amount of compensation and awarded Rs.1200/- per Are for non irrigated land.

3. Learned Advocate for the appellants pointed out the judgment of this Court passed in First Appeal No.932 of 2018, Prakash Vishwanath Akat Vs. The State of Maharashtra and Others with connected appeal dated 19.09.2024 as well as the judgment in First Appeal No.1141 of 2018 dated 04.04.2022 , wherein this Court awarded compensation as under:

 (ii) Rs.3,750/- per R for semi irrigated land.
 (iii) Rs.5,000/- per R for irrigated land.
 (iv) Rs.1,250/- for barren / pot kharab land.
4.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate for the appellants prayed to award the compensation to the claimants as per the rate of irrigated lands held above, as their acquired lands are irrigated.
He pointed out 7/12 extract of block no.40, which shows that there is a common well.
The 7/12 extract of the block no.41 also shows that there is a well and motor pipeline.
For block no.41, the Special Land Acquisition Officer has awarded compensation for well.
He further submitted that block nos.39 and 40 are owned by the one and same family members and therefore, both the lands are irrigated.
However, the learned Reference Court has not appreciated the said evidence in its proper 27-fa-759-2013+ perspective and awarded inadequate compensation to the appellant.
He therefore prayed to allow the appeals on the principle of parity by awarding compensation at the double rate of the dry land i.e.5,000/- per Are.

5. Learned AGP for the respondent-State and learned Advocate for the respondent-Acquiring Authority strongly opposed the appeals and submitted that the claimants failed to establish that their acquired lands were irrigated.

They pointed out the reasons and findings recorded by the learned Reference Court as well as the crop statement of the acquired lands for the relevant years, wherein it is shown that Jowar (Sorghum), Hybrid Jowar (Hybrid Sorghum), Kardi, etc were cultivated.
It is contended that the nature of crops grown clearly indicates that the lands were not fully irrigated.
They lastly prayed to dismiss the appeals.

6. Upon perusal of the Record and Proceedings, particularly 7/12 extracts and in view of law laid down in the judgment of Chindha Fakira Patil (D) through L.Rs. Vs. The Special Land Acquisition Officer, Jalgaon, reported in MANU/SC/1282/2011, it is held that even if the crops like sugarcane, wheat, etc., are not cultivated by farmer when water facility is available, the said land shall be treated as irrigated.

entities.text: L.Rs. Vs. The Special Land Acquisition Officer, Jalgaon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph 13 is as under:
13.
The High Court was also not right in upsetting the finding of the Reference Court on the issue of the nature of 27-fa-759-2013+ land.
In his deposition, Arjun Sukhdeo Patil categorically stated that there were wells in the lands of the Appellants and there were Jujubee, Tambrine, Mango, Pomegranate trees.
This was supported by the entries contained in 7/12 extracts.
The High Court discarded the evidence of the Appellants by observing that they had not cultivated sugarcane and wheat.

When it was not in dispute that there were wells in the acquired land, there mere fact that the Appellants had not cultivated sugarcane or wheat cannot lead to an inference that the land was not irrigated and, in our view, there was no valid reason for the High Court to interfere with the finding recorded by the Reference Court that parts of the lands were Bagayat and for such land they were entitled to compensation @ Rs. 6 lacs per Rangnath Shamrao Akat vs The State Of Mah And Ors on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52012153/
3 hectare.

entities.text: Rangnath Shamrao Akat vs The State Of Mah And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Considering above ratio and on perusal of the 7/12 extracts, it is clear that the claimants' acquired lands were fully irrigated except five Are land and therefore, they are certainly entitled to the enhancement in compensation @Rs.5,000/- per Are in view of judgment of this Court passed in First Appeal No.1141 of 2018 on the principle of parity.
The First Appeals deserve to be allowed.
Impugned judgment and awards deserve to be partly set aside.

Hence, the following order:
ORDER a.
Both the First Appeals are allowed.

b. Impugned judgment and awards are partly set aside and modified as under:
i.

The Claimants are entitled for the enhanced amount of compensation @Rs.5,000/-
per Are for their irrigated acquired lands, and Rs.1250/- for barren/Pot Kharab lands which 27-fa-759-2013+ includes earlier amount received by them alongwith all the statutory benefits like additional component, interest and solatium on the said amount, etc. as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
c. It is clarified that the claimants shall not be entitled for the enhanced amount of compensation for the period of delay, if any condoned by this Court.
d. Acquiring Body shall deposit the enhanced amount of compensation in this Court within twelve weeks from the date of receipt of this judgment.

e. On depositing the said amount and upon payment of deficit Court fees, if any, for enhanced amount of the compensation be paid to the appellants/claimants accordingly.
f. Pending Civil Applications, if any, are disposed of.
(SANJAY A. DESHMUKH, J.) Rushikesh/2026
